subject: Urban Planning
title: Age-Friendly Cities: Designing for Aging
description: Learn Age-Friendly Cities: Designing for Aging in one minute.

hook.text: By 2050, 2 billion people will be over 60. Most cities are designed for young, able-bodied drivers. That's a problem.

buildup.text: Seniors need walkable streets, accessible transit, nearby healthcare, and social spaces. Suburban sprawl isolates them.

discovery.text: The WHO's Age-Friendly Cities network designs for aging — benches every 100 meters, wide sidewalks, and senior-accessible housing.

twist.text: In car-dependent suburbs, seniors who can't drive become prisoners in their own homes. They lose independence overnight.

climax.text: Dense, walkable, transit-rich neighborhoods are naturally age-friendly. The best city for a senior is the best city for everyone.

punchline.text: Design for the oldest resident. Everyone benefits.

quiz.question: Why does suburban sprawl harm elderly residents?
options: Suburban property taxes are too high for fixed-income seniors
Car-dependent design isolates seniors who can no longer drive safely
Suburban homes are too large for elderly residents to maintain
